## Verified this step (measured, reproducible)

1. **The filed dominant hypothesis is implausible.** Autonomous sessions spawn
   with `permissionMode: bypassPermissions` (`spawn_session.py` L1970, L2388-94,
   L2597), so a genuine permission PROMPT is unreachable in the affected
   sessions. The observed "user doesn't want to proceed" rejection text is how
   a never-completed PreToolUse gate is recorded at session stop, not evidence
   of a dialog. The PreToolUse-hook path is the surviving mechanism: a
   PreToolUse hook runs BEFORE the tool launches, which is exactly why even
   the instant background "Async task launched" ack never arrived.

2. **PreToolUse guard-hook cost scales with argv size — measured.** Feeding the
   real Step 10d gate body (extracted verbatim from SKILL.md, 26,478 bytes /
   412 lines) to each of the 9 PreToolUse Bash hooks as PreToolUse JSON:

   | argv bytes | guard_repo_root_branch | guard_tmp_tmux_sweep | guard_root_code_commit |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | 22 (control) | 0.12s | 0.08s | 0.08s |
   | 3,587 | 1.48s | 1.34s | 1.31s |
   | 13,929 | 8.00s | 6.43s | 7.30s |
   | 26,478 (real gate) | 17.16s | 12.94s | 15.81s |
   | 52,957 | 42.42s | 27.81s | 30.39s |
   | 105,915 | 66.72s | 39.02s | 48.14s |

   The other 6 hooks stay under 0.1s at every size. Scaling is
   linear-to-mildly-superlinear. Mechanism: these guards (2,464 / 379 / 1,916
   lines) split the command into clauses, then fork `printf | grep -qE` pairs
   and awk char-scans PER CLAUSE — a 412-line body becomes hundreds of clauses
   x several process spawns each. At the real gate size that is ~17s (max
   single hook) to ~46s (sum) of pre-launch latency per dispatch.

3. **No hook carries a `timeout`** — re-verified across all 16 Pre/PostToolUse/
   Stop entries; only `SessionStart` has one (15s). So ANY hook stall is
   unbounded by construction. This is the load-bearing finding: it makes the
   wedge unbounded regardless of which stall mechanism dominates.

4. **Prong 1 is both NARROWER and DIFFERENT from the filing.** #2005 already
   landed the detached script-file gate shape, so "pin the gate to the detached
   shape" is done. The RESIDUAL is that the launcher still embeds the whole
   multi-KB body in the Bash argv via a `cat > "$LINT_GATE_SCRIPT" <<'EOF'`
   heredoc (SKILL.md L11812-11817; same at L13887-13893) — and guards scan the
   whole argv INCLUDING heredoc bodies. So the 26 KB still gets scanned even on
   the "fixed" shape. Composing the gate script with the WRITE tool instead of
   a Bash heredoc drops the argv to ~60 bytes and removes the cost at source.
   This is the rule CLAUDE.md ALREADY mandates for `post-marker --file`
   ("compose that file via the WRITE tool, never a Bash heredoc — the guard
   scans the whole Bash argv including heredoc bodies", #1756); the gate recipe
   simply never adopted it.

5. **Prong 3 unaddressed** — no watcher lane keys on a pending `tool_use` with
   no `tool_result`; the only `tool_result` reference is a delivered-prompt
   classifier helper (`autonomous_session_watch.py` L3263-3266).

## Refuted this step

**git index-lock blocking is NOT the unbounded factor.** `guard_root_code_commit.sh`
does make live git calls against the shared root per gated path (L1167-1202:
`diff --cached --name-only`, `ls-files -s`, `hash-object`), so a lock-contention
stall was the leading candidate. Control test in a throwaway repo with
`index.lock` held: all three READ ops returned in 0.00s (rc=0); only the WRITE
op failed, and it failed FAST (rc=128). Read ops do not take the index lock.
Branch closed.

## Residual gap (plan-time item, not a blocker)

Measured hook cost at the real gate size is tens of seconds; the observed
wedges were 1.2-2.4h. The duration is NOT reproduced. Surviving candidates:
(a) fork amplification under fleet load — these guards spawn hundreds of
processes each, and the VM runs ~15 concurrent sessions (cf. #2039's loadavg
~20 threshold, #2054's measured ~6x contention penalty); (b) an
input-dependent unbounded loop in a guard (`guard_tmp_tmux_sweep.sh` L90 has a
`while :;` parse loop). Prong 2 makes the residual moot rather than requiring
it to be solved: a bounded hook converts an unbounded wedge into a loud
failure. The plan should NOT block on reproducing the full duration.

## Prong re-ranking for the planner

1. **Hook timeouts** (was prong 2) — promote to FIRST. Smallest diff, bounds
   the failure class regardless of mechanism, independently valuable.
2. **Gate argv shape** (was prong 1, redirected) — compose gate scripts via
   Write, not a Bash heredoc; removes ~46s/dispatch and the scan surface.
   Drop or allowlist the `sudo -n choom` prelude is a SEPARATE, smaller item
   (denied anyway, FAIL-OPEN by design, and NOT the cost driver — measured).
3. **Watcher pending-call lane** (was prong 3) — keep last; it is the backstop
   that catches whatever 1+2 miss.

## Critic BLOCKER — upheld (verified independently)

The critic argued A1 is answered against the plan by the official hook docs.
Orchestrator verified at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, verbatim:

- `timeout` common field: "Defaults: 600 for `command`, `http`, and `mcp_tool`".
  So a hook timeout is NOT absent — v2's claim "unbounded by construction
  because no hook carries a `timeout`" is WRONG. The absent SETTINGS field
  means the 600s DEFAULT applies, not that no bound exists.
- Timeouts section: "A timed-out `command`, `http`, or `mcp_tool` hook doesn't
  block the tool call. The call continues through the normal permission flow,
  so don't count on a stalled hook to act as a gate."

So prong 1 as specified in v2 is a SECURITY REGRESSION, not a fix: lowering a
fail-closed guard's timeout from 600s to 60s makes the guard render no decision
~10x more cheaply, and the call then proceeds. The guards it would have been
applied to are the repo-root branch fence and the root-code-commit gate. v2's
pre-registered change-my-mind condition (§0.0) has FIRED. Prong 1 is DROPPED.

## Critic MAJOR 2 — partially refuted (orchestrator correction)

The critic inferred a duration candidate of "9 sequential 600s cancels ~= 90
min, inside the observed 1.2-2.4h band". That does not hold: the same docs page
states "All matching hooks run in parallel." The hook phase wall is therefore
max(hooks), not the sum. The same correction applies to the ORCHESTRATOR's own
v2 §2 figure — "~46s (sum)" is wrong; the correct cost at the real gate size is
~17s (the slowest single hook). v2 §2 is corrected in v3.

## New probe — lingering-children hypothesis REFUTED

With cancellation bounded at 600s and fail-open, a multi-hour wedge requires
cancellation to be INEFFECTIVE. Leading candidate (critic MAJOR 2(i)): the
fork-heavy guards leave grandchildren holding the write end of the hook's
stdout, so a caller reading to EOF never returns.

Probe (`/tmp/issue2115_cancel_probe.py`): launch each slow guard in its own
process group with stdout on a pipe, feed the real 26,478-byte gate argv,
SIGTERM the LEAD process only after 2s, then measure (a) surviving descendants
and (b) whether the pipe reaches EOF.

| guard | tree at kill | survivors | pipe EOF | wait |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| guard_repo_root_branch.sh | 1 | 0 | yes | 0.00s |
| guard_tmp_tmux_sweep.sh | 1 | 0 | yes | 0.00s |
| guard_root_code_commit.sh | 1 | 0 | yes | 0.00s |

Cancellation is CLEAN: zero survivors, immediate EOF. `tree at kill = 1` also
shows the guards fork SEQUENTIALLY (one child at a time), not a fan-out that
could linger. Hypothesis refuted.

## Consequence — the task's premise is re-scoped

Four candidate mechanisms have now been excluded under control:

1. Permission prompt — sessions run `bypassPermissions` (Step 1).
2. git index-lock blocking — read ops do not take the lock (Step 1).
3. Hook cost unbounded — 600s default cancel, hooks in parallel (this round).
4. Cancellation defeated by lingering children — clean cancel (this round).

With hooks bounded at ~600s per dispatch and failing open, **the guard-hook path
cannot account for a 1.2-2.4h stall.** The measured ~17s cost is real but is not
the wedge. The stall therefore sits OUTSIDE the hook phase — in the
harness/transport layer, which this repo does not control.

That inverts the plan's value ordering:

- The watcher pending-call lane (v2 prong 3) becomes the PRIMARY deliverable: it
  detects the wedge regardless of cause, which is exactly the right instrument
  when the cause is outside our control surface.
- The gate argv shape (v2 prong 2) stays, re-framed honestly as a LATENCY /
  hygiene fix worth ~17s per dispatch that also applies the already-canonical
  #1756 Write-tool rule to the gate recipes — NOT as the wedge fix.
- Hook timeouts (v2 prong 1) are DROPPED for cause (fail-open semantics).

## Ask 2 — "Hook timeouts" — DELIBERATELY NOT DONE (dropped for cause)

Body asked: add explicit `timeout` fields (~30-60s) to every PreToolUse /
PostToolUse hook entry in `.claude/settings.json` so a hung hook fails loudly
instead of wedging forever.

**This would have been a security regression, and the premise behind it is
false.** Both halves were verified against the official hook docs
(https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), quoted verbatim in the `epm:critique`
marker:

- The premise "no hook carries a timeout, so a stall is unbounded" is WRONG: the
  `command`-hook `timeout` default is **600s**. An absent settings field means
  the default applies, not that no bound exists. Matching hooks also run in
  **parallel**, so the hook-phase wall is max(hooks), not the sum.
- A timed-out PreToolUse command hook **"doesn't block the tool call. The call
  continues through the normal permission flow, so don't count on a stalled
  hook to act as a gate."** So lowering these guards from 600s to 60s would make
  them render no decision ~10x more cheaply — and the guards in question are the
  repo-root branch fence and the root-code-commit gate, both fail-closed
  security surfaces. By the measured cost curve, any argv at/above ~50 KB (or
  the real 26 KB gate under fleet-load amplification) would routinely exceed a
  60s timeout and silently skip the guard.

`.claude/settings.json` is therefore UNTOUCHED (confirmed: it is absent from the
8-file diff). The plan recorded this as its pre-registered change-my-mind
condition firing, and the implementer brief explicitly forbade re-introducing it
so it could not creep back in.
